title: Seat the water bottle in the side-entry cage of a small frame
instruction: Put the water bottle in the bottle cage on the bike frame so the cage holds it, then let go.
context: Riders put a bottle in a frame cage before most rides. On small frames the top tube sits so close above the cage that the bottle cannot go in along the cage's own axis, and side-entry cages are sold for these frames: the bottle has to get past the cage's sprung arm, end up resting on the cage floor, and the hand has to get back out of the closed frame triangle. The frame here is a full-size replica of a real extra-small frame's front triangle carrying the real cage.
setup: World: x away from the robot, y to its left, z up; bench top z 0.7475 m. Fixture: a full-size replica of a Salsa Rangefinder XS front triangle (tube centrelines from the maker's 1:1 drawing) in 6061 aluminium round tube: down tube 2 in OD in two straight pieces 193 and 410 mm, top tube 1-3/8 in in two pieces 211 and 217 mm, seat tube 1-3/8 in 378 mm, head tube 2 in 95 mm; joints clamped between 12 mm plywood gussets. Its plane is at x 0.430 m, head tube to the robot's left, tipped 10 degrees nose-down, the bottom bracket's underside 40 mm above the bench on a plywood block and the head tube on a 45 mm post, on an 18 mm plywood board 240 x 620 mm. Cage: Elite Custom Race X (74 mm, 147.3 mm tall, 28.5 g, black glass-fibre polyamide), bolted into M5 rivet nuts at the down tube's upper two boss positions (64 mm apart), floor 35 mm below the lower bolt (estimate); the cage axis slopes 51 degrees from level, the floor's middle at (0.430, -0.515) m, 250 mm above the bench; 8 mm from the bottle to the down tube (estimate); 60 to 70 mm of room above the seated bottle's cap. Its side toward the robot is open; a sprung front arm (a band 48 to 88 mm up, hinged on the far front, wrapping 40 degrees past the front toward the robot) closes over the near side of a seated bottle. Bottle: Elite Fly Tex 550 ml, empty, cap shut: 74 mm across, 184.5 mm tall, 51 g, blue with a white cap in the simulation (the listing linked in README.md is the red one; the colour plays no part), lying on its side on the bench. Lot A: base centre at (0.250, -0.300) m, cap toward +y. Lot B: base centre at (0.300, -0.170) m, turned 25 degrees anticlockwise seen from above (cap toward the robot's left and toward the robot). Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Build files: fixture/frame-fixture-1to1.svg (1:1 drawing with a 100 mm check bar) and fixture/cut-list.csv; README.md has the bill of materials with sources and the build steps.
scoring: Per trial, every credited state needs both hands more than 5 mm from the bottle and the cage's front arm and the bottle and arm still within 1 mm for 1 s (real trial: video). 1.0: bottle seated, its base rim within 1.0 mm of the cage floor along the cage axis (a 1.0 mm feeler gauge cannot be passed under the rim all the way round), base centre within 3.0 mm of the cage axis (ruler, in end photos square to the cage from the front and from the open near side, against centre marks made at set-up on the cage floor's edges; the two offsets combined as the sides of a right triangle), axis within 3 degrees of the cage's (phone inclinometer on the bottle and on the down tube), and the front arm within 5 degrees of shut (its tip within 6 mm of a tape mark at its rest position, by ruler). 0.5: inside the cage behind the shut arm but not seated (bottle axis within 6 mm of the cage axis at the arm's band, read from the same two photos 68 mm up the cage; within 10 degrees by inclinometer; base rim at most 30 mm above the floor by ruler). 0 otherwise, including held, outside or leaning on the arm, upside down or on the bench. Whole trial: if the front arm is ever bent open more than 30 degrees (slow-motion video against a card marked at 30 degrees behind the arm's tip), or the hands, bottle or cage cannot be read at any step, the trial scores 0. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 1,000 control steps (50 seconds at 20 Hz) per trial; trials on lots A and B, averaged (--epochs 2).
reset_notes: 1. Pull the bottle out of the cage sideways toward the robot (the arm springs open and shut). 2. Lay it on its side on the bench at the lot's tape marks: lot A base centre (0.250, -0.300) m, cap toward the robot's left; lot B base centre (0.300, -0.170) m, turned 25 degrees anticlockwise from lot A. 3. Check the cage arm is shut and the fixture is on its marks. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: True-size frame replica (gusseted tubes, curved lower down tube made straight; tipped 10 deg nose-down as in a repair stand) with the real cage and bottle; tubes are octagonal prisms; rigid bodies, real contact. Cage flex is one hinged front arm on a torsion spring; its 1.3 N closed / 3.9 N at 15 deg tip forces, wall shapes, cap size and 35 mm floor offset are estimates to measure. Bottle body is a 16-sided prism and does not squeeze.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 (lot A 1.0, lot B 1.0). Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lot A 0.0, lot B 0.0; step limit both). object_jitter=0, --epochs 2.
